blocks.content: A node reporting NotReady is a whole-machine problem, not a single Pod issue, and Kubernetes deliberately waits before rescheduling its workloads, to avoid overreacting to a node that is merely slow, not actually gone.
1. The Whole Node, Not Just One Pod
blocks.text: 1. The Whole Node, Not Just One Pod

blocks.content: This is a genuinely different scale of problem from everything else covered in this module, a NotReady node affects every Pod running on it simultaneously, not one isolated workload.

blocks.alt: Every Pod on the node affected at once, not a single, isolated issue

blocks.content: The kubelet itself may have crashed or become unreachable (covered in the Architecture module), a genuine network partition may have isolated the node, or the node may be under real disk or memory pressure, several distinct, genuine root causes.

blocks.alt: Several genuinely distinct root causes, each affecting the whole node

blocks.content: kubectl describe node includes a Conditions section reporting exactly what is wrong, memory pressure, disk pressure, or a general readiness failure, stated explicitly.

blocks.alt: The exact condition stated explicitly, not something to infer indirectly

blocks.content:
kubectl describe node node-3
# Conditions:
#   Type             Status
#   MemoryPressure   True
#   Ready            False

code.content:
kubectl describe node node-3
# Conditions:
#   Type             Status
#   MemoryPressure   True
#   Ready            False

codes.bash:
kubectl describe node node-3
# Conditions:

blocks.content: This is exactly the self-healing mechanism covered in the ReplicaSet & Replication module, once a node is genuinely confirmed unavailable, its Pods are rescheduled onto healthy nodes elsewhere.

blocks.alt: The exact self-healing mechanism covered earlier in this course, now applied at node scale

blocks.content: 5. Why There Is a Real Delay First
blocks.text: 5. Why There Is a Real Delay First

blocks.content: This is a deliberate, important design choice, Kubernetes waits a real, meaningful window before treating a node as genuinely gone, protecting against evicting and rescheduling everything just because a node was briefly slow to report in, not actually dead.

blocks.alt: A deliberate safeguard against overreacting to a merely slow, still-alive node

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A NotReady node is a whole-machine problem, kubectl describe node's Conditions section states the exact underlying issue directly.
Kubernetes deliberately waits before rescheduling that node's Pods elsewhere, a real safeguard against overreacting to a node that is merely slow, not actually gone.
